financing.summary: Tri Pointe stopped being a public company on May 14, 2026, when Sumitomo Forestry (Tokyo: 1911) bought it for $47.00 a share in cash; it is now a wholly owned subsidiary of Sumitomo Forestry America and still files 10-Qs only because its two senior notes series remain outstanding. At September 30, 2026 it carried $1,103M of homebuilding debt ($300M of 5.25% notes due June 2027, $350M of 5.70% notes due June 2028, a $450M bank term loan due 2027) against an undrawn $850M revolver, $325.9M of cash and about $1.1B of liquidity. It controls 32,444 lots, 51% owned and 49% controlled; of the controlled lots about 10,000 are under option or purchase contracts ($225.9M of deposits against $1.89B of remaining purchase price) and 5,758 sit in unconsolidated land development joint ventures. Its use of land banking is small but real and recent: a first land bank financing arrangement ($19.6M of proceeds in 2025), credit-facility covenants rewritten in April 2025 to carve out lot sales under land banking arrangements, and disclosed land banking options that oblige it to finish development work even if it walks away; no land banker is named in any filing. The room for a land banker turns on the new parent: cash fell by $657M in nine months as inventory grew by $512M, about $750M of Tri Pointe debt comes due between June and September 2027, and Sumitomo Forestry's one-year JPY 835.1 billion SMBC bridge loan (sized to include an assumed refinancing of Tri Pointe's debt) falls due May 10, 2027.
financing.land_strategy: Mixed, roughly half owned and half controlled; the company does not use 'land-light' language or publish an option target. The FY2025 10-K says it buys most land under purchase agreements that are often structured as options so takedowns can be staged, uses joint ventures, options and land banking 'if necessary', and routes every acquisition through a centralized land committee. Sumitomo Forestry told analysts in February 2026 that the lot position (then 32,738) was roughly half owned and half optioned and a healthy level, and that as a public company Tri Pointe's growth investment had at times been limited by share buybacks, which ownership by Sumitomo removes.

lots.source_title: Tri Pointe Homes Q3 2026 results press release (8-K Exhibit 99.1, 2026-11-05), Lots Owned or Controlled table
lots.note: By segment (owned / controlled / total): West 8,896 / 3,594 / 12,490; Central 5,609 / 7,801 / 13,410; East 2,178 / 4,366 / 6,544. At 2025-12-31: 15,954 owned / 16,265 controlled / 32,219 total. 'Controlled' means lots under land option contracts or purchase contracts and includes the company's expected share of lots owned by unconsolidated land development joint ventures: 275 in West and 5,483 in Central at 2026-09-30 (zero and 5,356 at 2025-12-31). Excluding those 5,758 JV lots, 10,003 lots are under option or purchase contracts (our subtraction). pct_optioned is our calculation (15,761 / 32,444). years_supply is our calculation, not a company figure: 32,444 lots over 4,197 trailing-twelve-month deliveries (FY2025 4,947 less nine months 2025 3,583 plus nine months 2026 2,833). Sumitomo Forestry's February 2026 briefing described the position as about six and a half years of supply on FY2024 volumes.

land_banking.counterparty: Undisclosed land banker (land bank financing arrangement, 2025)
land_banking.description: Tri Pointe sold land under a land bank financing arrangement and kept an option to buy it back, so the sale is booked as a financing: the land stays on the balance sheet as consolidated inventory not owned. The cash flow statement shows $19.6M of proceeds from the arrangement in 2025 and none in the first nine months of 2026.
land_banking.source_title: Tri Pointe Homes Form 10-K for fiscal year 2025 (filed 2026-02-26), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows
land_banking.note: First appeared in Q3 2025: no such line in the Q1 2025 cash flow and inventory not owned was all deposits at 2025-06-30; $12.8M of proceeds by 2025-09-30 and $19.6M for the full year. Consolidated inventory not owned was $19.6M at 2025-12-31 and $14.4M at 2026-09-30 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1561680/000156168026000047/R10.htm). Counterparty, lot count, location and pricing are not disclosed. No comparable line in 2023 or 2024.

land_banking.counterparty: Undisclosed land bankers (option-based land banking arrangements)
land_banking.description: The variable interest entity note says Tri Pointe has entered into land banking arrangements under which it must complete the development work even if it terminates its option to buy the land or lots. These sit inside its option agreements with unconsolidated VIEs; the land banking share is not broken out.
land_banking.source_title: Tri Pointe Homes Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 (filed 2026-11-05), Note 6 Variable Interest Entities
land_banking.note: Option agreements with unconsolidated VIEs (land bankers and other sellers together): $215.4M of deposits and $1,817.3M of remaining purchase price at 2026-09-30 ($201.6M and $1,960.5M at 2025-12-31). The same sentence appears in the FY2025 10-K. The April 30, 2025 credit agreement modification changed financial covenants to exclude the impact of lot sales under land banking arrangements (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1561680/000156168025000062/tph-20250430.htm), and the debt note describes interest incurred as covering 'all debt and land banking'. No counterparty is named.

land_banking.counterparty: Land sellers and developers under option and purchase contracts (not named)
land_banking.description: All land and lot option and purchase agreements together: $225.9M of non-refundable deposits securing $1,886.6M of remaining purchase price at September 30, 2026, covering about 10,000 controlled lots outside joint ventures.
land_banking.source_title: Tri Pointe Homes Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 (filed 2026-11-05), Note 6 Variable Interest Entities
land_banking.note: Split: unconsolidated VIEs $215.4M deposits / $1,817.3M remaining price; other option agreements $10.5M / $69.3M. At 2025-12-31: $209.6M deposits / $2,069.4M remaining price. Capitalized pre-acquisition costs $12.5M. lots (10,003) is our subtraction: 15,761 controlled lots less 5,758 JV lots, from the Q3 2026 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1561680/000156168026000044/tphex991q32026.htm). Option abandonment and pre-acquisition charges were $13.5M in the first nine months of 2026, including a $9.0M Q2 charge for optioned lots in one West community that the company chose not to buy. Some sellers are master developers with repurchase rights (FY2025 10-K).

land_banking.counterparty: Unconsolidated land development joint ventures (partners not named)
land_banking.description: Tri Pointe counts its expected share of lots owned by unconsolidated land development joint ventures as controlled lots: 5,758 at September 30, 2026 (275 West, 5,483 Central, the segment covering Texas, Colorado and Utah). That is 37% of all controlled lots, held off balance sheet with partner capital and JV-level debt.
land_banking.source_title: Tri Pointe Homes Q3 2026 results press release (8-K Exhibit 99.1, 2026-11-05), footnote to Lots Owned or Controlled table
land_banking.note: 5,356 lots (all Central) at 2025-12-31. Partner names, which projects, and the takedown terms are not disclosed. See joint_ventures for the JV balance sheet.

debt.instrument: PARENT LEVEL (Sumitomo Forestry Co., Ltd., not a Tri Pointe obligation): acquisition bridge loan, up to JPY 835.1 billion
debt.source_title: Sumitomo Forestry: Notice Regarding the Conclusion of a Loan Agreement with Financial Covenants (2026-05-07)
debt.note: Yen loan signed May 7, 2026, drawn about May 11, bullet repayment planned May 10, 2027. JPY 835.1 billion is the maximum and, by Sumitomo's own footnote, includes funds for the assumed refinancing of Tri Pointe's existing debt on top of the roughly JPY 630 billion share price. Covenants: consolidated and parent net assets at least 75% of the prior year, and an R&I issuer rating of BBB- or higher. Sumitomo says it will refinance into long-term funding within about a year; JPY 350 billion of hybrid bonds and a subordinated loan were raised in September 2026 toward repayment (see capital_events). The balance still outstanding today is not disclosed in the notices read.

capital_events.description: Fifth Modification to the credit agreement: revolver raised from $750M to $850M with an accordion to $1.2B, maturity extended to April 30, 2030 with three one-year extension options, and financial covenants changed to exclude the impact of lot sales under land banking arrangements.
capital_events.note: The land banking carve-out is the first sign in the filings that Tri Pointe was preparing to sell lots to land bankers; the land bank financing arrangement followed in Q3 2025. Agent: U.S. Bank National Association.

capital_events.description: Board raised the 2025 share repurchase authorization by $50M to $300M.
capital_events.source_title: Tri Pointe Homes Form 10-K for fiscal year 2025 (filed 2026-02-26), Item 5
capital_events.note: The $250M program had been authorized on December 18, 2024 and ran through December 31, 2025.

capital_events.description: Sixth Modification: term loan facility increased from $250M to $450M and split into Tranche A (matures September 29, 2027, two one-year extension options) and Tranche B (matures June 29, 2027).
capital_events.note: Effectively a $200M debt raise: the 2025 cash flow shows $201.6M of borrowings from debt. Tranche B was $35.0M at signing and $10.0M by year-end.

capital_events.description: First land bank financing arrangement: land sold to a land banker with a repurchase option retained, booked as a financing. Proceeds were $12.8M by September 30, 2025 and $19.6M for the full year.

capital_events.note: Counterparty not disclosed. Date is the quarter the line first appears (Q3 2025).

capital_events.description: Full-year 2025 repurchases: 8,550,822 shares for $277.2M at an average of $32.42, leaving $22.8M of the authorization. No shares were repurchased in 2026.
capital_events.source_title: Tri Pointe Homes Form 10-K for fiscal year 2025 (filed 2026-02-26), Item 5
capital_events.note: Q4 2025 alone: 1,575,362 shares for $51.2M. Cumulative through June 30, 2025 was 5,458,694 shares for about $175.0M (corrected in an 8-K filed 2025-07-25). Buybacks ended with the merger; Sumitomo Forestry has said the capital will go to growth instead.

capital_events.description: Merger agreement with Sumitomo Forestry at $47.00 per share in cash (about $4.5B transaction value, $4.1B equity value). Sumitomo obtained a debt financing commitment for the yen equivalent of $5.4B; no financing condition.
capital_events.note: Values are from the joint press release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1561680/000119312526049867/d75298dex991.htm). The price was a 29% premium to the prior close and 42% to the 90-day VWAP. The lender was not named in the 8-K; Sumitomo's May 7 notice names Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation.

capital_events.description: Seventh Modification: U.S. Bank as agent and the lenders consented to the Sumitomo Forestry merger, waived the resulting default, and rewrote the Change in Control definition around Sumitomo's ownership. The revolver and term loan stayed in place.
capital_events.note: Stockholders approved the merger the same day; the HSR waiting period also expired April 16, 2026 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1561680/000119312526160387/d110756d8k.htm).

capital_events.description: Parent level: Sumitomo Forestry signed a one-year bridge loan of up to JPY 835.1 billion with Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation to fund the purchase; the amount includes funds for an assumed refinancing of Tri Pointe's existing debt.
capital_events.source_title: Sumitomo Forestry: Notice Regarding the Conclusion of a Loan Agreement with Financial Covenants (2026-05-07)
capital_events.note: Amount is in yen (not converted here). Planned repayment May 10, 2027. As of September 30, 2026 Tri Pointe's own notes and term loan were still outstanding, so the assumed refinancing had not happened.

capital_events.description: Merger closed: Tri Pointe became an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Sumitomo Forestry, was delisted from the NYSE and deregistered. Sumitomo put the price paid for the shares at about $4,003M.
capital_events.source_title: Sumitomo Forestry: Notice Regarding the Completion of the Acquisition of Shares of Tri Pointe Homes (2026-05-14)
capital_events.note: Tri Pointe booked $79.7M of transaction expense and $122.2M of merger-related G&A in the first nine months of 2026 and reported a net loss of $127.3M for the period. Closing 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1561680/000119312526222960/d317054d8k.htm

capital_events.description: Parent level: Sumitomo Forestry drew a JPY 106.5 billion subordinated syndicated loan (Tranche A JPY 69.0 billion due 2062, Tranche B JPY 37.5 billion due 2064) to repay part of the Tri Pointe bridge loan.
capital_events.source_title: Sumitomo Forestry: Notice on Execution of Syndicated Loan Agreement with Subordination Provisions (2026-08-31)
capital_events.note: Signed August 31, 2026. Expected 50% equity credit from R&I and JCR. Lenders not named.

capital_events.description: Parent level: Sumitomo Forestry issued JPY 243.5 billion of publicly offered hybrid (subordinated) bonds in three series (JPY 130 billion at 3.310% due 2061, JPY 63.5 billion at 3.824% due 2063, JPY 50 billion at 4.343% due 2066) to repay part of the Tri Pointe bridge loan.
capital_events.source_title: Sumitomo Forestry: Notice on Determination of Issuance Conditions of Publicly Offered Hybrid Bonds (2026-09-04)
capital_events.note: With the subordinated loan this makes JPY 350 billion of hybrid funding, the total Sumitomo targeted on August 7, 2026 (https://sfc.jp/english/news/pdf/20260807_Notice_on_Issuance_of_Publicly_Offered_Hybrid_Bonds.pdf). Lead manager Daiwa Securities; joint leads SMBC Nikko, Nomura and Mizuho. Rates shown are initial rates. That leaves a large part of the JPY 835.1 billion bridge still to be termed out by May 2027.

joint_ventures.partner: Not named (17 unconsolidated partnerships and LLCs)
joint_ventures.description: Equity investments in 17 active homebuilding and land development partnerships or LLCs at September 30, 2026, with ownership of 8% to 50% and no controlling interest. Tri Pointe's investment was $232.5M; the entities held $929.2M of assets ($897.8M real estate) and owed $294.0M of debt.
joint_ventures.source_title: Tri Pointe Homes Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 (filed 2026-11-05), Note 5 Investments in Unconsolidated Entities
joint_ventures.note: Up from 15 entities, $183.1M invested and $177.6M of JV debt at 2025-12-31. Tri Pointe put $75.1M into the entities in the first nine months of 2026 (against $36.2M a year earlier) and received $36.2M back. Tri Pointe and sometimes its partners guarantee parts of JV loans (completion, remargin, environmental); no liability is recorded. Outside partners' equity was $367.3M.

joint_ventures.description: Unconsolidated land development joint ventures supply lots to Tri Pointe: its expected share was 5,758 lots at September 30, 2026 (5,483 in the Central segment, 275 in West), counted in controlled lots.

key_metrics.source_title: Tri Pointe Homes Q3 2026 results press release (8-K Exhibit 99.1, 2026-11-05)

ma.counterparty: Sumitomo Forestry Co., Ltd. (through Sumitomo Forestry America, Inc.)
ma.description: All-cash acquisition of 100% of Tri Pointe at $47.00 per share, announced February 13, 2026 and closed May 14, 2026 by reverse triangular merger with Teton NewCo, Inc. About $4.5B transaction value; Sumitomo put the price for the shares at about $4,003M at closing.
ma.map_impact: Ownership changes from Public to subsidiary of a foreign company; parent is Sumitomo Forestry (Tokyo: 1911) via Sumitomo Forestry America. The spine row still shows Public. Tri Pointe keeps its brand, its Irvine home office, its 17 divisions and its management (CEO Doug Bauer and President and COO Tom Mitchell per the closing release; Glenn Keeler signed the November 5, 2026 8-K as CFO); the five outside directors named in the closing 8-K resigned. It becomes a second US platform beside Sumitomo's five existing builders (MainVue Homes, Bloomfield Homes, Brightland Homes, DRB Group, Edge Homes); Sumitomo says it has no plan to merge the platforms now. The group claims a pro forma rank equal to fifth in the US, about 15,000 homes a year across 18 states and roughly 114,000 lots. For financing: capital decisions now run through a Japanese parent that funds in yen, buybacks have stopped, and public lot and debt disclosure will end once the 2027 and 2028 notes are repaid.
ma.source_title: Tri Pointe Homes 8-K (completion of merger), filed 2026-05-14
ma.note: after_ranking is true because the deal closed on May 14, 2026 and the closing release already cites the 2026 Builder 100; it was announced on February 13, before the ranking. The Builder 100 row (4,947 closings in 2025) is Tri Pointe standalone. Tri Pointe's president received a $10.9M retention bonus at closing; the CEO, CFO and general counsel also have retention agreements dated February 13, 2026. Advisors: Moelis and Paul Hastings for Tri Pointe; Mitsubishi UFJ Morgan Stanley / Morgan Stanley and Morrison & Foerster for Sumitomo. Sumitomo said talks with Tri Pointe's founders ran for about two years. Per the merger proxy (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1561680/000119312526110678/d114079ddefm14a.htm), the CEOs first met on May 16, 2024; Sumitomo bid $41.00 on December 1, 2025 (rejected), $45.00 on December 11 and $47.00 on January 16, 2026; the board did not solicit other bidders.

gaps: Land-banking counterparties: not publicly disclosed. The filings confirm a land bank financing arrangement (2025) and option-based land banking arrangements but name no land banker, lot count or program size.

Links to Domain Real Estate Partners, Millrose Properties, Kennedy Lewis or TPG Angelo Gordon: none in the SEC filings and Sumitomo Forestry documents read. The press search by firm name (also DW Partners, Essential Housing, IHP Capital, Brookfield, Varde, Oaktree, GTIS, Hearthstone, Walton, Forestar) was not run.

Credit ratings (Moody's, S&P, Fitch) for Tri Pointe: not stated in the filings opened, and rating-agency releases could not be searched for. Left blank rather than filled from memory. Parent-level: Sumitomo Forestry's bridge loan requires an R&I issuer rating of BBB- or higher.

Whether Sumitomo Forestry will refinance, guarantee or repay Tri Pointe's 2027 notes, 2028 notes and term loan: not disclosed. The bridge loan was sized for an 'assumed refinancing' of Tri Pointe debt, but all of it was still outstanding at September 30, 2026 and no intercompany loan or parent guarantee appears in the Q3 2026 10-Q notes.
Joint-venture partner names (17 unconsolidated entities, including the land development JVs behind 5,758 controlled lots) and the financial services JV partner: not publicly disclosed.

Individual lenders in the U.S. Bank-agented credit agreement, the mortgage warehouse lenders, the senior notes trustee and whether the credit facility is secured: not captured from the documents read (the modification agreements are exhibits that were not opened).

Tranche A term loan amount ($440.0M) is derived, not stated. Years of lot supply (7.7) and lots under option excluding JVs (10,003) are our calculations. liquidity_usd_m (1,148.7) is cash plus revolver availability; the company rounds it to 'approximately $1.1 billion'. total_debt_usd_m (1,158.3) includes $54.9M of mortgage repurchase borrowings; homebuilding debt is $1,103.4M and homebuilding debt-to-capital 25.9%. net_debt_to_capital_pct is the company's net homebuilding debt-to-net capital ratio (3.5% at 2025-12-31).
Lot split between finished-lot options and raw land purchase contracts, and lots by state or division: not disclosed (segment level only).

M&A by Tri Pointe as acquirer in 2025 or 2026: none appears in the FY2025 10-K cash flow statement, the 2025 to 2026 8-K list or the Q3 2026 10-Q. Trade press was not searched for small unannounced deals.

The Q3 2026 10-Q MD&A (land spend, covenant actuals at September 30, 2026) and the Q3 2026 earnings call were not read: the main filing document truncates before MD&A and the notes were read through the filing's R pages instead. Tri Pointe's own investor site now redirects to a short page on tripointehomes.com with no debt or ratings information.
Current balance of Sumitomo Forestry's bridge loan after the September 2026 hybrid financings, and its plan for the remainder before May 10, 2027: not disclosed in the notices read.
